definition: In multi-armed bandit problems, IMED (for Indexed Minimum Empirical Divergence) is an algorithm developed in 2015 by Junya Honda and Akimichi Takemura.
details: It is the first algorithm proved to be asymptotically optimal respect to the problem-dependant Lai–Robbins lower bound for distributions in ( − ∞ , 1 ] {\displaystyle (-\infty ,1]} .
story: Imagine a video game where the only feedback is the score ticking up or down — and you learn by playing a million rounds. Instead of being told the rules, it discovers them by living with the consequences. The machine is not handed the answers — it tries things, earns a reward or a miss, and slowly figures out what works. Reward, not instructions, is the teacher. That learn-by-reward loop is Algorithm IMED.
